utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams, I notice only the absence of Mr. Bourgon. Madam Nikolic, he was supposed to be returning today, Monday. Will he be showing up later?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Obviously, some unexpected problems have arisen. I think I have a problem with my interpretation. I can't hear. Just a moment. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Check that you are on the right channel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. From the Prosecution side, I notice the presence of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls. The witness, Mr. Erdemovic, is present already. I take it that there are no preliminaries so we can proceed. Yes, Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, just a few questions. On that 10th of July, in the evening hours, when you came to the elevation overlooking Srebrenica, during that afternoon, late afternoon, evening and night, there was no combat activity, was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we got to that elevation, as I said, we passed by the UN check-point and we could see some houses had been burned, and it was obvious there had been combat during the day, but that night there was nothing -- no shooting to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us through which place did you pass?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I remember I came from the south side of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I put it to you that the only populated area through which you could pass from the south side was Slapovic, which is not on the road and it was not burned down. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot know exactly through which place we passed. I told you already that when we passed by the UN check-point and we were going towards Srebrenica, some houses were burnt and you could see there was -- there had been combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, in that locality, some combat activities did take place but earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "earlier"? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1993, in that locality, serious battles took place between the 28th Division and the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it. I don't know exactly. I wasn't there, but I know that there was combat between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the VRS in the environs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you allow the possibility that the damage you saw resulted from that earlier combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but some houses were still burning. They can't have been burning from 1993 on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, you entered the town. Was it before or after NATO air strikes?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After. If I remember correctly, we were already moving towards the town. We had not yet arrived. We had just descended from that elevation down the slope, going towards town, when we heard that NATO aircraft had dropped one or two bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As you were descending into town, there was no fire opened at you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was sporadic shooting. I cannot tell you exactly now but, yes, there was shooting; not much but there was some.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: But there was no artillery fire from either side?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's just that, at one moment, the Praga was used by the VRS because somebody had said that sniper positions were detected at some position, and there was sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the town itself, there was no artillery fire on the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You said that the flag from the mosque was removed by Velimir Popovic. The mosque was undamaged?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was nothing wrong with the mosque, only the flag had been removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, is the name Dragan Todorovic familiar to you? Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the name; but maybe if you showed me a picture, I could remember the face, if I know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you need a photograph, 1997, on which we can see three members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, a photograph on which you identified two men? Do you need it to identify the third person?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me who is the third person on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to say; but if you insist that I identify the person, I can give you his name.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number because 1997 seems to be a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. 1981. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I do insist on an answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. His name is Zeljko, and I don't know the last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The witness showed some reluctance last time, if we are talking of the same person, on the basis that according to him this man did absolutely nothing illegal. I'm trying to use his same terms. And that he was quite friendly with the witness. I think we ought to give the witness the option of mentioning his name in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. You've mentioned one part of his name already any way. Go ahead, Mr. Erdemovic. Who is the third man? Zeljko what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know his last name, Your Honour. I just know his first name. His name was Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Unless there has been some changes, I have Mr. Krgovic who wishes to cross-examine this witness, and I think Mr. Meek or Mr. Ostojic. Do you wish to go first? Okay, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. We have entered into a stipulation with the Prosecution on two specific points that we were going to question this witness on. In light of that, we will not have any questions for this witness today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we will be filing the stipulations immediately after the close of court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Ostojic, and thank you, Mr. McCloskey, as well. So Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Will you start answering please only when I turn off my microphone? As long as you see the red light, don't answer or say anything.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back, briefly, to the question asked by my learned friend Mr. Petrusic. When you arrived on the 10th to that elevation overlooking Srebrenica, it was in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all happened in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You answered to my colleague, Mr. Petrusic, a question about combat on the 11th. I have the same question about the 10th. There were no exchanges of artillery fire or any other fire on the 10th before you set out for Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And from the position where you were, you could see the town and you could see the extent of shelling on the town, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there was none? There was no shelling in that period from the 10th all the way until the 11th when you entered the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no shelling of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you entered the town of Srebrenica, you did not see any major damage, craters from shells. You didn't see any serious damage to the town. You had been in Vukovar in 1991 and you know what a town that was shelled looks like. Compared to Srebrenica you could determine that there had been no shelling?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You could not -- there is no comparison between Srebrenica and Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Krgovic. In the meantime, for the record, Mr. Bourgon has entered the courtroom. For the record, also, I do not have on my list any other Defence team that wishes to cross-examine this witness. So unless I hear anything different, I'll proceed to ask Mr. McCloskey if he's got re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions. Mr. Erdemovic, I'm not sure whether the Prosecution had asked this or not. Can I ask whether Mr. Pelemis was aware of what you did in Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know of the way command was exerted over our unit, he did know. I'm 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell me the basis upon which you say so?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not a single action or mission of our unit was possible without the knowledge of the commander of our unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Major Pecanac? Was he also aware of what you did?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, yes, they had to know. Pelemis -- I don't believe Pelemis would have done anything without them knowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my last question is about Zeljko, whose name you revealed today. My question is how he was able to keep himself from what you guys were doing, things that were not permitted, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, it wasn't only Zeljko. In Vlasenica, there were people from Vlasenica and people from the Bijeljina platoon; and if we were between 30 and 40, in total, only eight of us were at that farm. So more than 30 persons were not involved in what we were doing, and I cannot explain why we were chosen to do what we had to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Kwon's last question was exactly one of the questions I wanted to ask you. But on the same -- in the same context, you've just confirmed that you were eight. There were eight of you in Branjevo Farm. I would like you to go through the names again one by one. I know that you have mentioned them, But what is more important for me is to know their ethnicity. You were, for example, a Bosnian Croat. Now, let's start with the other seven, one by one, and please tell us their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko Boskic, Bosnian Croat; Franc Kos, Slovene; Golijan, a Serb from Vlasenica; Brano Gojkovic, a Serb; Stanko Savanovic, a Serb; Aleksandar Cvetkovic, Serb; and Zoran --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last name of Zoran?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Zoran who?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Goronja, a Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There being no further questions, your testimony finishes, ends here, Mr. Erdemovic. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and I also wish you a safe journey to wherever you're going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. McCloskey, documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There is a sheet, and I believe I've mentioned each on that sheet. I didn't get into the detail of the plea agreement, but I think it's a good thing that you have that; otherwise, that's everything on the sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from any of the Defence teams? I don't think we have a question of translation here either. So not hearing any objections, all these documents are being admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, just the plea agreement did not have a 65 ter number, but I spoke to the Defence about that earlier and they had no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey, and thank you also all the Defence teams for being practical about this. Ms. Nikolic, you made use of an OTP information report which you would like to tender. It has 65 ter number 1D285. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections from Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or any other of the Defence teams, for that matter? Okay. So it is so admitted. Thank you. And we can move now to the next witness, who I hope is here. And we are talking of witness to be precise, number 142, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he has no protective measures, to my knowledge, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could be excused for just one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. McCloskey. Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence; and before we move ahead with your testimony, you are required under our rules to make a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is being handed to you now. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn commitment with us that you will be telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Make yourself comfortable, please. Take a seat. I suppose you already know what's going to happen. Mr. Nicholls, for the Office of the Prosecutor, will be putting some questions to you. He will then be followed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He will then be followed by the various members of the Defence teams on cross-examination. Your duty is to answer each and every question fully, and to the point, and truthfully, irrespective of who is questioning you. So, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. One point, I apologise for not raising this earlier, I've explained to the witness his rights under Rule 90, but I think perhaps the Court should advise him and I think my friends would agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hear no comments from the Defence teams. Make it a rule to advise us on this because we are never really, unless we are talking of a Rule 92 bis or 92 ter witness, we would not be in a real situation to make a proper assessment. So you need to bring this to our attention, you and any of the Defence teams for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry I didn't do that first thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. Mr. Bircakovic, you've heard what Mr. Nicholls has just said, and the indication also is that you have been made aware of the existence of certain rights that you enjoy as a witness under our Rules. One of these rights pertains to everybody's right not to be forced to incriminate oneself. It may well happen, although I'm not saying that it will, that questions may be put to you or will be put to you, that, if answered, could possibly expose you to criminal proceedings, to incriminate you, in other words. Now, in conformity with the application of the principle world wide, we give the witness in such circumstances the right to ask to be exempted from answering such questions. This right is not an absolute one, however. It depends on our assessment of the circumstances. We may well decide to grant you an exemption, to dispense you from answering such questions, or we may decide to compel you, to order you to sense such questions nonetheless. If we do so, if we compel to you answer such questions, then you enjoy another right, a consequential right; namely, that anything that you would say in answering such questions, because you are compelled to answer such questions, shall not be used as evidence against you in an a subsequent -- in any subsequent Prosecution that might be taken against you, except if the Prosecution or the proceedings are for false testimony, which I hope will not be the case. So have I made myself understood to you? Have I explained your rights clearly enough for you to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think on the basis of that we can proceed. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll be asking you a few questions as I explained to you yesterday. Listen to the question carefully, think and try to remember carefully, and answer as best you can. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Actually, it was Saturday, not yesterday that I spoke to you. Could you tell the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Milorad Bircakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you have any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you ever known by any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I was younger, perhaps. They used to call me Pinjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: In Grbavci, on the 6th of August 1963.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And very, very briefly, could you tell us what your current occupation is? What do you do now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, currently I work in the factory in Birac, near Zvornik, as a worker on assembly line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us when you were mobilised into the VRS in 1992, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised, together with the others, on the 6th of April 1992, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And which brigade were you part of in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was a member of the Territorial Defence, and later on, of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In 1993, which unit of the Zvornik Brigade were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: First, I was a member of the village company, and later on I was transferred to serve as a member of the tank crew in n the tank company. Later on I was a member of the Drina Wolves for a while, and I ended up as a member of the military police of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you end up as a member of the military police of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this may have been sometime in 1993, towards the end of 1993 or in 1994, thereabouts. I wouldn't be able to give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And in July 1995, were you still a member of the Zvornik Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, where -- when you were a member of the military police - this is a quick question - where were you stationed in 1995? Where were you based?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: We were stationed in the barracks, maybe two kilometres away from Zvornik, that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's the Standard Barracks at Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you know an officer named Drago Nikolic in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was his position then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Security affiliated with the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you ever work directly with Drago Nikolic in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver, his driver, Drago's driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And by July 1995, how long had you known Drago Nikolic? How long had you worked with him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe a year or so, from 1994, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, do you also know an officer named Miomir Jasikovac in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Military Police Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who did he report to, Jasikovac? Who was above him in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe to Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Finally on this point, also in July 1995, did you know an officer named Milorad Trbic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was his position then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the Deputy Chief of Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, an officer named Vujadin Popovic, did you know him in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Security of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, finally, Ljubisa Beara, did you know him in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Security of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to jump ahead now to 14 July 1995, and ask you some questions about that day. Approximately, when did you go on duty that day, 14th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just so we know, when did you go off duty the previous night, the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where did you spend that night, from 7.00 to 7.00, over the 13th to the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the morning of the 14th of July, after you came on duty, did you receive any orders as a driver?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What were your orders?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was ordered to go and pick up Drago Nikolic at the forward command post, and I was supposed to bring him over to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Trbic, the Deputy Chief of Security, gave me that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just for the record, where was that forward command post that you went to pick up Drago Nikolic or that you were ordered to go to pick up Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately, some 15 kilometres from the Standard barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was the name of the town or the area where the IKM forward command post was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the name is Jerkici, one part of the Kitovnice village area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why were you supposed to go and get Drago? What was he supposed to do when he came back to the command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was supposed to attend a meeting with Beara and Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you go to the forward command post to pick up Drago Nikolic, as ordered?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went there and I brought him back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What time did you leave Standard, and what time did you get back to Standard for the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was maybe half past 7.00 or 8.00. I wouldn't know exactly, and I returned maybe half an hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we'll get to the logs later, but which vehicle, which car, were you driving when you went to pick up Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: An Opel Rekord.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What colour was that Opel Rekord?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was neither green nor blue. The car was not very specific, bluish, greenish.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what model of car shape was it? A station wagon, two door, four door, five door, three door? Can you describe the car a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Five doors, a caravan, a station wagon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just if you can help me explain, do you know what an Opel Kadet looks like from that time period?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it had five doors. I don't know what you mean. How do you mean this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My question was really just whether you remembered. What I'd like you to do is explain how, if you're looking at an Opel Rekord or an Opel Kadet from then, how do they look different or how do they look the same? Can you describe the differences or the similarities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we are looking at an Opel Kadet Caravan and Opel Rekord, then the two would be very similar. The difference would be minor. The headlights are the same on both cars, if we are talking about the station wagon with five doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, coming back to when you returned to Standard with Drago Nikolic, where did he go in the command? What happened when you got back from picking him up?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He went to his office to attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you do during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the command, I had an office which served as a cafe place where coffees were made for officers and others, and this is where I was sitting while the meeting was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long was the meeting, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, maybe 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after the meeting, did you see Drago Nikolic again?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how did he appear when he came out of the meeting? What was his mood?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Somber. He was not in a good mood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did he tell you that his orders were or his tasks now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. He did not tell me anything about his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did he say you were going to do when he came out of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Beara --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I object to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Mr. Meek, sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object to that question. It's repetitive. It's been asked and answered. All the Prosecutor is trying to do is ask the same question the witness just answered no to. He didn't tell him anything about any task, and now he's just going around it in the back-door fashion. I object to that strenuously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's two completely different questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Still, his answer on line 23, in answering your question, "No. He did not tell me anything about his orders." And then your question was: "What did he say you were going to do when he came out of the meeting?" So it refers to him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm asking -- maybe I can make it clearer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What I'm asking is what did Drago Nikolic say that you and he were going to do after he came out of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't you simplify it and say, All right. He didn't tell you anything about his orders. Did he tell you anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did Drago Nikolic say to you when he came out of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I object to that question. It assumes facts not in evidence. There is no evidence that he's told him anything. It's a leading and suggestive question to suggest that Drago Nikolic said anything to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's being asked whether he told him anything else. I mean, the witness has already affirmed that there were no explanations on orders, but there may have been other conversations. So go ahead. Answer the question, please. What did Drago Nikolic say to you when he came out of the meeting? Obviously, if he didn't say anything, you will answer he didn't say anything. But if he said something, you need to tell us what he told you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as he came out of the meeting, he did not say much. We started walking to the car, ready to leave. And then he told me that I was supposed to drive him to the Vidikovac hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Then we arrived at Vidikovac hotel, and then buses arrived with prisoners on board.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where is the Vidikovac hotel in relation to Zvornik? Can you just describe -- I think you can describe easily where that hotel is located.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The hotel is about two kilometres away from Zvornik towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did Drago Nikolic tell you was going to happen at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he did mention anything to you, you need to tell us. If he didn't, obviously, you say that he didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At first, he did not say much. We came up there, and maybe a couple minutes later the buses arrived. After that, however, he told me that I should get on the first bus because he would take the car to do some errands. I got on the first bus. He took the car, and he drove away in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: First of all, how long were you and Drago Nikolic at the hotel Vidikovac that morning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: We were in front of the hotel, and we stayed there maybe only five minutes or so, not longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long was -- were there buses already there, or did the buses come after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The buses arrived maybe five minutes later, five minutes after us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Approximately, what time of day is this now that the buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe half past 8.00 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How many buses arrive at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell. The road is very curvy, it meanders, and I could see as far as five or ten buses. I don't know exactly, but I didn't pay too much attention to the whole situation any way. The road is really very curvy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who were on these buses, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were security guards on board, and there were also men, Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Drago Nikolic told you to get on the bus; is that right? What you said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who told the bus drivers where to go next? Where did they -- who directed the bus drivers what they should do next, after they gathered at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were in a convoy. They already knew where they were going. Nobody told them where they should go from that place. I suppose that they had known already. Nobody asked any questions so I suppose that they already knew where they were headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So, when you got on the bus, did you know where you were going, where the bus you were on was going? Think.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew from the moment they left Karakaj that they were going towards Tuzla. I was familiar with the road. I didn't know exactly where they were heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you got on the bus, you had no idea where that bus was going to stop that you were on?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where did the bus -- where in the column was the bus that you got on to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the first bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where did the bus go?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: First towards Tuzla and then the primary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you familiar with that school? Had you been there before?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew it because I attended that school, from year five to year eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Describe what happened when the buses arrive at the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the buses arrived, then the prisoners were ushered into the gym by the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Approximately, how many prisoners? I know you can't give me an exact number.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think four or five buses arrived. They were not quite full, but how many people could have been on four or five buses? Perhaps 200.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After those four or five arrived. I know you talked about there was a curve in the road, and it was hard to know. After those four or five arrived, did you see any more arrive at the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived, together with the convoy of buses, there were four or five buses. I don't remember the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I asked you if more buses came and you said not then. Did more buses arrive later?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: At the school, besides the prisoners and the security on the bus, who else was there, if anyone, when you arrived, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a lot of local population there. Whether the military police arrived at that moment, whether they were among the guards who secured the location, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember specifically any Zvornik Brigade military police being there? I mean individuals.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Trbic was there; Cedo Jovic; Goran Bogdanovic; there were some military policemen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember if there were any women policemen there, military police personnel?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Her name is Nada. I'm not sure about the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have any relatives who were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Stanoje Bircakovic, nicknamed Cane.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether he was at the Orahovac school that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, what about the commander, Miomir Jasikovac? Did you see him at the school that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When? When did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw him there from the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you just describe briefly how -- or what happens with the prisoners on the buses? I think -- I can't remember if you've answered that. I'm sorry. What happened to the prisoners on the buses after you got to the school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: They were ushered into the gym of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you said there were Serb local civilians present? What were those local civilians doing? I'm not speaking about Muslims, but Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. They were simply curious to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you got on the bus at the hotel Vidikovac and Drago Nikolic took your car, the Opel Rekord. When is the next time you see Drago Nikolic? After leaving the Vidikovac hotel, when is the next time you see him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe around 11.00, because I didn't keep the exact time. It could have been 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where did you see him around 11.00 on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He came to the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did he get to the school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: By car, the one that I drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Same car?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, same car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did he do when he got to the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He got out of the car, gave me the car keys, and then he went out there, talked to Jasikovac, other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you go into the school or into the gym at any time where the prisoners were kept?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When Drago Nikolic gave you the keys to the car, did he say anything to you? Did he say anything at all to you or he just handed you the keys and didn't say a word?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He gave me the keys, saying, "Take the keys," turned around and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long, roughly, was Drago Nikolic at the school that -- at that time, around 11.00, that you were aware of? How long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe an hour. I can't know exactly because nobody was timing things. I can give you rough times but no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand you didn't have a stop watch with you. Now, after that, when is the next time you see Drago Nikolic again?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He came just before night fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Came where?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: To the school again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We talk about that a little bit later. After you get off the bus at the Orahovac school, and then some time later, around 11.00, Drago Nikolic comes and stays for an hour, that you see, what are you doing this whole time? What's your job?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I was standing there. There was this road going uphill. I was standing by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you said Drago Nikolic was there for about an hour around 11.00. Where did he go or what did he do after that hour? What happened next with Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He went somewhere. I wasn't paying attention. He just left. He wasn't there any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who did he leave with?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, he left you the car. Do you know how he left the school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, during that day, did you see any other VRS officers at the school? You've already talked about some.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when was that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps half an hour or an hour after the prisoners were brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you speak to Popovic when he came?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did he do that you could see?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was standing by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he have any officers with him or was he alone?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There were two more. Whether they were security or whether it was his driver, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you see Popovic speaking to any of -- anybody else at the school, any other officers or soldiers there, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember. When I noticed him, he was standing with those two men of his. I wasn't really observing to see whether he talked to someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said well, "I think it was Popovic." Why did you say you think it was Popovic? Are you sure, not sure, how sure, that it was Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: 99 per cent, let's say, because I know -- I know it was that officer I saw, and I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And could you tell me his position one more time, as you recall what it was at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was Chief of Security for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you see any officers more senior at the school that day, more senior than Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions now about how the prisoners came to leave the school. Can you describe that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning, a smallish truck arrived and took away those people who were outside the school. It would reverse, back up towards the door, people were loaded, and then it went; and then after a while, another truck came.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you know, do these trucks have a name? Can you describe the trucks any more?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were trucks covered with tarpaulin, smallish ones, used for procurement. We called them small TAMs. They have a box of four metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, could we have a little break of not more than two minutes? You could all simply stay here, and a little bit please. Thank you. --- Break taken at 10.19 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you describe, please, a little bit more, how the prisoners actually got on these trucks? You said -- I think you said they were loaded or put on the trucks. You said, "the people were loaded." How were they loaded?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: They got in, one by one, on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about their hands? Were they bound in any way or were they free to use their hands to get on the truck?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The hands were tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you recall, if you do, whether or not there were blindfolds placed on the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the start, but later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, again, approximately, how many prisoners would board one truck for one trip? How many prisoners could fit in the back of one of these TAM trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if it was four metres long, then perhaps 20, 30. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when the trucks were full and they left, which direction did they go? Where did they go after pulling out of the school yard?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: It went towards Krizevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was there any escort for these trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the outset, no. But maybe after two or three trips, I was told to follow the trucks to a fountain. Taking the asphalt road, I should turn around by the fountain and go back to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Who was it who told you to do this, to follow the trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Jasikovac maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did you do after Jasikovac told you to follow these trucks to the water point?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I followed the truck to the fountain where I would turn around and go back; whereas, they continued on. From that point on, it was a macadam road, still good enough for a TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, line 5 of page 30, his answer to your question that "Jasikovac, maybe." He needs to tell us whether he knows it was Jasikovac or whether he has got big doubts as to who possibly could have ordered him to follow the trucks up to the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Think again, Witness, try to remember - you heard His Honour's question - who it was that told to you follow the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was Jasikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, who else would it have been at that time there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Trbic was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But to the best of your memory, it's Jasikovac who ordered you? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how many times did you make this trip? How many trucks full of prisoners did you follow up the road?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe four or five times, I went after them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Would it help you to -- do you have any trouble remembering that? Would it help to you look at your statement about how many times you went? It's not a huge difference.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't you put the question straight to him? Could it be seven, eight, ten? I don't know what he said in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In your statement, you said five, six, seven. You weren't sure but about five, six, seven. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Around that number, four, five, six. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What vehicle were you using when you followed this truck-- these trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: That Opel Rekord that I drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you have any weapon with you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: My own side-arm, the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you have any other weapon with you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we are taking the break at the normal time, this would be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls, and thank you, Witness. We will take a 25-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me go back one minute, Mr. Bircakovic. When the prisoners were loaded on to the trucks, did they leave any belongings behind or did they take anything with them, or what happened to any personal belongings they might have had?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any clothing or anything left behind?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: When they first arrived, and as they got off the buses, they had a surplus of luggage which they left behind in one part of the courtyard, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, could we have 65 ter number 1700 on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph, Witness. I hope this works. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the left image and bring that up a little bit more? Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Take a look at that photograph, sir, for a minute, and tell me if you recognise the place we see there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know because I've already seen this photo. This is a photo of the road leading to Krizevici. Up there, you can see the railway tracks; and above the railroad tracks, this is where the bodies were buried. This is where the grave was, and here you can see the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that in a minute. Can you -- looking at this, can you tell where the water point or fountain is located on this photo, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The water source is on the main road before the road forks off towards the railroad, some three or four metres before that, on the road leading to Krizevici, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose you need the assistance of Madam Usher, so that he places a marking on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was just going to ask, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, could you --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Look at it carefully and see if you can tell the main road and the railroad tracks and where the water point was. Perhaps -- let me show you the whole photo again, and see if that helps you recognise the area we are in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could scroll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. There is a mark over there, which I suppose needs to be deleted for the time being. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, you mean the mark the witness just made?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was a mark but he made it before the question was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This mark? This red mark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No. He had the question asked to him, and he answered by putting the mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He explained where the fountain was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then he put the mark before he was asked to. Let's keep it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at this carefully. What have you marked there with the red? What is that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a water well there, and I went up to the water well in the car. I was following the lorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now I'd like to scroll to the right, if we can, and show the witness the whole photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think we have to first log this in. He needs to put a W. Write W next to that spot, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And put your signature or your initials and today's date, please. Today is the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So let's mark that. Now, proceed as you wish, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. If I could have this again so that I could move it and scroll? Thank you. All the way to the right. Continue, please. Okay. Maybe if we make it just a little bit smaller. That's good, and could we go a little bit further to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you've recognised this road as a road to Krizevici. Can you tell, looking at this, which is the road and which is the railroad track?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the road, and the railroad track is above that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And what is this -- continuing over to the right, what is that building complex there? We could blow that up a little bit on the right-hand. Do you see this -- if you look at the right of your screen, Witness, you see next to the top line.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is that there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the railway station on the railroad track, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what is the building there? That's the railway station, you think. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's mark them, please. Let's start with the small dot to the right of the picture, the photo, which you put next to a group of buildings there. Could you please write RS next to that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you could please mark and try to think about it carefully, which one -- put an RR next to the one which is the railroad track that you think. Try to think carefully about it and look at the picture, if you need to.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then could you put your initials on the bottom and the date?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. His Honour asked you if you could please put an RS next to what you believe to be the railway station?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will need to mark this in the first place, but I would like to proceed further on this matter. Let's mark it. Save it, yes. Thank you. Now, Mr. Nicholls, or Madam Registrar, if we could zoom in the last frame; that is, the one to the right. No, no, that's to the left. It's the last one, yes. If we could zoom further. Okay. Stop, stop, stop. Now, looking at this frame, Witness, you see a group of buildings at the top of the picture and another building on its own towards the bottom. Do you know what that building at the bottom of the picture -- what it represents? What building it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you mark, again, on this photo the road which you followed and the railway track and the railway station again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the road. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you write R, please, next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And the railway track?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Railway track now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the previous photo back, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But we need to cancel this for the time being. Go back to the previous one, and we return to this later. Is there any objection? Okay. So let's cancel what he's just written for the time being. Let's go back to the previous.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we could zoom in on both ways?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Is that enough, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I wonder if we can even zoom more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Zoom more, zoom more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: More. Once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This looks like a river to me, and this is the road. [Marks] But I don't know whether this up there is the railway station or maybe the school in Krizevici. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, looking at this photo in front of you, the top line and the other line which you just marked, which one appears to have tracks on it, to you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The lower one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, think again. Try to see if you were mistaken. Which one is the railroad and which one is the road? And I'll ask if houses are normally closer to a road or to a railroad track.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Around the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So which one do you think is a road and which one do you think is the railroad tracks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this should be the railroad track, and above it should be the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just mark what you just now said you think is the railroad track to be clear as RR?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And now could you mark -- just write RD on what you believe is the road?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could give that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just not to leave any marks unmarked or not identified. That other line that he put on the -- he marked on the photo and said it's probably the river, if he could write -- do you still believe that that is where the river was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So could you write RV, please, next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's mark this one. You still don't know what the building next to what you've marked now as the railway track was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's save this one, please. You need to put your initials and date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, let's zoom out or move to the left. Further, further, further, further, further. Last frame. Yes, here. Now, could I ask you to mark again where the well -- where the fountain was, please? Now, following the two tracks that you have indicated, the upper one would be the normal road and the lower one would be the railway track. So where do you think the fountain was situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, I think. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you write W, please, next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And your initials and date, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you need this photo any further for the time being?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then don't save it for the time being, please, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that when you were following the trucks with prisoners, were you told to turn around at the water point. And you've just indicated where the water point was, and you said that the trucks ended up going up a non-asphalt road or used a dirt road or something that was suitable for TAM trucks. Which way did the trucks go from the water point after you stopped and turned around? If you need -- well, you can't blow it up. But if you need more time to look at it, let me know. From the water point, where did the trucks go?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived up at the fountain and the lorries went on, driving on the same road. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've just indicated an arrow in the direction that the trucks took?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And you maybe just put a T by that arrow?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I think we could save this now, Your Honour. I'm done with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, during this process where the prisoners are taken away up the road, after it starts, you said you started following the trucks, what did you hear going on in the location where the trucks were taking the prisoners up that dirt road? What sounds did you hear, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I accompanied the lorries to that fountain, I turned around in the car and went back. On that day, there was shooting. There were rifle shots on the frontline which I could hear. This was like a corridor that they had to go through, the Muslims, and I could hear rifle shots, shooting. The car engine was on so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But also when you were back at the school, could you hear shooting before you started taking these trips, when the first trucks went and came back?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There were rifle shots, even when I returned to the school. When I escorted the buses, I could hear rifle shots and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The transcript says "buses." Is that correct? Was it buses or trucks you were escorting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. How many times -- you said you went up four, five, six, seven times, how many cycles -- how many trips did these trucks make when they went up the road to the water point, turned left, and then came back for more prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, four, five, six times. Every time, there were two lorries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did you think was happening to the prisoners who were taken up that dirt road? What did you conclude after a while was happening to them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: At first, I didn't know anything until the very end, until I could see the dead finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what did you conclude was happening?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening, when I and Drago went to the forward command post to pick up his things, it was already dark. When he arrived at the school, it was already dark and he told me that we should get his stuff at the forward command post; and as we were passing by that road, in the headlights, you could see people -- people's bodies lying around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we'll get to that. But is that the first time that you thought that an execution might be taking place, or did you think that any earlier, when you heard those shots and the trucks coming back empty?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I might have suspected something. I wasn't 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you know any of the drivers of the trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw one, and I knew him. I know his name only. His name is Rajko, but I don't know his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what battalion was he in? What unit?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the 4th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have any discussions with him that day while he was driving these trucks or in between his drives?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. They worked all the time. The lorries' engines were never turned off, and the drivers remained in the lorries and nothing was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Gojko Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him from the frontline, from 1992, when I still went to man the line on Parlog, the so-called Parlog line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where was he on the 14th of July 1995? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, around 12.00 or maybe 1.00 or even 2.00 - I don't know exactly - he came to the line -- actually, on his way to the line, on foot, he came up to the school. That's where I saw him, by the school. I don't know what happened to him next, whether he did end up on the line or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what unit was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The same, the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me again about when Drago Nikolic -- when you saw him again that day. Where exactly did you see him, and as close as you can, what time was it when you saw him? You started saying you saw him at the school, and then I said we would talk about it in a little while. I want you to talk about it now, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came to the school, but that was already before night fall. In fact, it was already night fall so I don't know what time it could have been. He stayed for half an hour, an hour, then he came up to me and said we were going to fetch his personal effects from the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And try to remember, you've just said before night fall or night fall. When was it? Was it dusk? Was it dark? And if it helps to you look at your statement, you can look at that. You talk about it. I think you talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Just before night fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you see who he spoke to during that half hour or hour that he was there on the second occasion, just before night fall?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He had company, but I don't know exactly who he was talking to. I cannot recall the name precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that he was talking to Jasikovac and Trbic. Does that help you to remember? That's at page 61.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly, possibly, he was talking to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, do you remember that or do you not remember it? Try to think carefully.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Jasikovac is a possibility. I'm not quite sure about Trbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, at any time during this day, when you were at the school or when you were driving up and down the road to the water point, did you see any earth-moving equipment, any heavy construction equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not before the evening, not during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And the evening, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the evening, already after night fall, it was completely dark. One --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand this. Could the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nicholls. The interpreters couldn't catch the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The interpreters didn't catch your answer. I was asking you about heavy construction equipment, earth-moving equipment. And you said "In the evening when it was dark," and then the interpreter didn't get the rest of your answer. What happened in the evening when it was dark?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: One machine arrived. We call it UT, something for loading earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if I could just check with the interpretation, is it UT or ULT?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: ULT, that's what we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you see this ULT?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Outside the school. He came and stopped outside the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it stayed for about five, ten minutes before it left in the direction of Krizevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be clear, that's the same direction the trucks left in, correct? You said that earlier.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you started talking earlier in an answer about how you took Drago Nikolic to the forward command post, and that's when you saw bodies. What did -- did Drago Nikolic say anything to you when he came back to the school the second time before you took him to the forward command post? What did he say to you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He did not approach me before the moment when we were supposed to go and fetch those things for him. At that moment, he just came up to me and said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He said, "Drive me to the AKM [as interpreted], the forward command post."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
