utterances.text: Now, please describe what you started to tell us about how you then saw bodies or concluded that an execution or you thought that an execution had taken place. Describe what happened and what you saw when you were driving to the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the left side, closer to the road, perhaps five metres from the road, I saw corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How many, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Forty, 50 maybe. That's what I saw by just glancing sideways. It's a small section of the road. You pass by in just a few seconds. That's what I could see in the reflection of the headlights.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, approximately, how close is this to that water point?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you say anything when you saw these corpses?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. We kept silent, both of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Both of you, meaning you and Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Right, nobody said a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long is the journey from the school to the IKM, to the forward command post, where you went to get Drago's things, Drago Nikolic's things?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe 15 to 20 minutes, max.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the IKM once you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't stay, but just a couple of minutes. The time it took him to get out, to fetch his things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what kind of things were these that he brought? I mean, personal, military, what kind of material was it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: His personal effects. He had a bag with toiletries that he took with him when he went up there, and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, on the way back, did you also go by the water point and the school and the bodies?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you see on the way back?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: The same thing we saw on the way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any activity around the bodies, any soldiers, any people who were alive?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And on the way back, did either you or Drago Nikolic say anything about these bodies that you said were close to the road?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: We did not discuss it at all because it's not something that you want to -- well, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Where did you go then? Where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: We went to the Standard barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Approximately -- did you stop anywhere on the way back from the IKM to Standard barracks? Try to remember.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. We went directly there, first, to fetch his things and then directly to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why did you take that particular route to Standard from the IKM?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was another macadam road, perhaps ten kilometres of macadam, but we didn't choose that one. I don't know now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you see going on at the Orahovac school when you drove past it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else happened. It was already dark, and there was almost no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, where is -- in July, 1995, do you know where Drago Nikolic's apartment was, where he lived?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where did he live then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: In Zvornik, in an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In Zvornik the town, or the municipality, or what?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What happened when you got to Standard that night with Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. Drago went to the office. I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What time was this approximately, as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it could have been 9.00. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, based on your experiences as a soldier in the Zvornik Brigade and as a MP, and from being there, do you think these killings in Orahovac, could that have been kept a secret from the Drina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why do you think it couldn't have been?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, because people from the Drina Corps attended meetings with Drago, and then Popovic was by the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions now about other places you drove in the following days. Tell me what happened, as far as you remember, on the 15th. Did you go back on duty on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you okay? Do you need a break?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You would like a break or you're okay?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want a break, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go ahead. Any time you need a short break, please don't shy away, tell us and we'll give you a break. The next break will be in three-quarters of an hour's time at 12.30. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Tell me about the next day, Witness, when you came on duty. As best as you can recall, what were your duties on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th, I think I drove Jasikovac to make an inspection of the battalion in Pilica, Lokanj. That's one battalion. On the way back, we passed by the school. We stopped by the school in Pilica, and that's where he stopped for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did you stop by the school in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was happening at the school there? What was the school being used for at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Prisoners were there, as well, in the school in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As best you can remember, were there any guards? Who were the guards guarding the prisoners, if you could tell?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, there were guards around, but I don't know where they were from because I was on the road, and I believe there is a hedge around the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you see what Jasikovac did there or who he talked to, what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He went there. I don't know to whom he talked. He went there to inspect, but I don't know who he talked to outside the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Try to send your mind back. I know it was a while ago. Did you see any corpses at the Pilica school, any bodies there at all?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I could see one body. You see, the school building has several storeys, and that man tried to run, jump out of the window, or I don't know what, and he lay there dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you see this happen, where the man tried to run or jump out of the window, or did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who told you about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a local man who told me that this man had tried to jump out of the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you later learn what happened to those prisoners in the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was also shown on TV, that they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you learn about it? I know it was on TV, but when did you just hear about it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that later, after the event. Maybe a month later, I learned about all these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere else that day besides Pilica, the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we dropped by Rocevic. There was also a school building with prisoners in it, and Jasikovac stopped by again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, was there anybody with you besides Jasikovac when you were driving to these places?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think Jasikovac was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any -- think carefully and try to remember. Did you see any -- besides Jasikovac, did you see any VRS officers on the road to Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think -- no. I don't remember if I saw any.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who -- if you know, who was guarding the prisoners? Who were guarding the prisoners at the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember which battalion was there, but there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I think you said it, but which brigade, although you didn't know the battalion? I heard it but it's not on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, may it please the Court, Your Honour, I object to that. It's been asked and answered. This is the second time. If you look at page 49, line 6, the question was asked, "Who was guarding the prisoners?" And he answered he didn't know because there was a hedge there and he was in the car. Now he has asked it again, and it's the third time. I object to repetitive questions because he didn't get the answers he liked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your comment on that, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He said, "There were guards around. He didn't know where they were from." That's not exactly the same thing as the question I asked to try to clarify this issue; and when he gave his answer to the question, it was not objected to. I heard him say "Zvornik Brigade," but it didn't appear on the transcript, which is why I asked that question again. And we are now at the Rocevic school, not the Pilica school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. This is what I was going to comment, actually. Because on page 49, line 6, we are still talking of the Pilica school. Now we are talking of the Rocevic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour. That was my mistake. I don't speak B/C/S but my Counsels do, and on another issue they said that what the Prosecutor is now insinuating the Witness did not say in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I asked him if he said, and you don't need B/C/S to understand, the word Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead with the question, limited to Rocevic, as you have already limited it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You did answer it again a second time; but can you tell me, Witness -- it didn't show up on the transcript, the second time. Could you -- which brigade were these soldiers from at the Rocevic school? Just for the record here, the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why do you say you think?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, because I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any one of them, any of those soldiers? Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know anyone personally. I mean I didn't recognise anyone I knew, but I suppose they were from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. What happened to the prisoners who were held at the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: They, too -- I mean, I heard that the same thing happened as in Orahovac and in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know where the Rocevic school prisoners were executed? Did you learn that later?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the stories went around later, in Kozluk, that they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, around this time, did you ever drive anybody to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the evening, when we returned from Rocevic, Trbic had been somewhere and it was late. There were no buses, and Trbic lived in Kozluk so I had to give him a lift that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After that day, when you drove Mr. Trbic to Kozluk, did you go by the execution site in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. This is going from Zvornik. It's at the entrance to Kozluk. His house was just at the entry point to Kozluk, maybe 20 metres from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were -- did you ever go by the execution site? Were you ever ordered to drive by that site with Mr. Trbic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in Kozluk, but once we went to Petkovci. Downstream from the dam, he went outside to look while I stayed in the car because stories were already circulating about these events. He got out of the car, inspected the situation, then we got back into the car and returned to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when was it that you went to the dam with Trbic and he went out and looked around, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe a month or two months after the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you go to any other sites, burial sites, execution sites, with Mr. Trbic, other than the ones you just told us about?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Orahovac and Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you know, if you know, what was Trbic looking for? What was he inspecting at these sites? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that he got out of the car, he looked around, and we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document now, 65 ter 296, on e-court, please. Now, looking first at page 1 in e-court, which is ERN number 00694699, take a look at that document on your screen and tell me if you recognise it. Tell me what it is.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a travel order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we see your name typed in the box, which on the English version, we can see is the names of the drivers. Who are these two people who have their names handwritten in?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Those are my colleagues who would work instead of me when I was off.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we see the vehicle make here is Opel Rekord, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 3 in e-court, please? Maybe blow it up. Thank you. All right. It is now 00694701.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's the same log, Witness. I've just jumped ahead a couple of pages. Do you see at the top, 14 July to 31st July 1995? What do those dates mean?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a travel order for the vehicle, for this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please, page 4 in e-court, 00694702.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, on Saturday, I showed you a copy -- I showed you this log, didn't I, when I met you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could -- first of all, the handwriting in column 4, whose handwriting is that? I have the original here if you need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Which is not yours, if you can tell?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that most, if not all of it, is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if we can scroll over to column 20, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Other than the last two signatures, who is signing in column 20, which is labelled, "User's signature"? Whose signature is that? I can give the original again if you need to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Those are Drago Nikolic's signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could scroll left, please, and if we could blow up the first heading, and first row, 14 July, 1995, if we could blow up column 4, please, and go to the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you just read me, in column 4, what the travel log says for where this Opel Rekord went on 14 July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: It says, "Standard, Orahovac, Divic, Orahovac, Zvornik, Standard, Loko, Karakaj," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you look at that again, please, the column. Do you see Rocevic there on the 14th? Doesn't it say Standard, Orahovac, Divic Rocevic, Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe this was for the other column.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just asking you what it says for the 14th. Does it say "Rocevic" there, because this is your handwriting, for the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: It says, "Standard, Orahovac, Divic, Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Doesn't it say, "Rocevic, Orahovac, Zvornik"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: It does say something to that effect, "Rocevic, Orahovac, Zvornik, Standard, Loko."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what does it say, Karakaj, then what, then Loko?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: "Karakaj, Rocevic, Loko, Standard, Zvornik." As I've already said, these travel orders do not reflect the reality of where the vehicle went and how it went. I've already spoken about that. They were not filled out really correctly. For example, in the first part, it doesn't say that I went to the forward command post on that day. Although, on that day, I did go to the forward command post. That's how things were done. For example, you would undertake a journey and you would enter just an approximate mileage that you did. For example, you would say Zvornik, Kitonjice, although you didn't go to Kitonjice, just to have something matching the mileage. What I'm saying is that these entries in one part are accurate, and the other they are not. For example, where it says Cer. Nobody went to Cer, but we missed four or five kilometres, and we decided which place was suitable fill that mileage travelled. That's why we entered Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, on the 14th, you've got down there, Orahovac. Did you go to Orahovac on the 14th? You've testified about that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about Divic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about Standard?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we blow that up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, according to this, where have you written that the car went on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Karakaj, Rocevic, Loko, Standard, Divic, Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And continuing down on the 16th, what do you have?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Standard, Zvornik, Standard, Rocevic, Kozluk, Loko; later on, Kula, Pilica, Loko, Loko, Standard, Kozluk, Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And in these days, did you -- is it accurate that you went to Rocevic, Pilica, Kula school, which you've talked about?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back a couple pages to the 13th of July, which should be page 2 in e-court, if we go down to the bottom there, the 13th of July, we have Standard, IKM, Zvornik, Loko, Orahovac, Zvornik, Orahovac, Standard, Bratunac, Zvornik. So I'm asking you now, try to think carefully and remember, did you go to Orahovac at all on the 13th of July, the day before, the night before the events you've talked about happening there on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember having gone there on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have one moment, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to go back now to just when you got on the bus at Divic. We are back to the 14th in the morning, and you went to Orahovac. Do you recall anybody telling you and the driver where the bus was going it? I want you to think carefully, and I can show you your statement, if it helps to you remember, if you're having difficulty remembering.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I believe that Drago had told me to get on the bus and go to Orahovac. This is where the bus was headed for, and I don't know about the driver. I did not talk to the driver at all. There were security guards on the bus who must have known where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But you remember Drago saying to you, "Get on the bus and go to Orahovac"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No further questions at this time, Your Honour. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I don't know if you have made arrangements amongst yourselves, the Defence teams, as to who is going first. Mr. Zivanovic, you asked for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. However, in the meantime, we have received additional information from the Prosecutor's Office, and that's why I would kindly ask you to prolong that time, based on the new information that we have received in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. You will have more time, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. On the 13th of March, 2002, you provided a statement to the investigators of the Prosecutor's Office. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on that occasion -- actually, I had an opportunity to see that the investigator warned you on several occasions that you were not obliged to talk to him, that it was in your best interests to speak the truth. Tell me, did you follow that advice?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew, I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that interview, did you receive a tape containing your interview? You were informed that the interview was recorded?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive the tape?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not receive the tape, but I did not even request the tape. I was told that if I wanted, I could get it and I did not deem important to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you receive the transcript, i.e., the written record of your interview?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not have an occasion to see it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, until I came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived here, did you listen to the tape or did you read the transcript of your interview?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you? Did it take you a long time to read it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Since I knew quite a lot, it took me a day or maybe a little bit longer to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were reading all day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe not the entire day, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention to some things that I noticed as being different from what you said on the 13th of March 2002, and what you have stated today. Did you yourself notice any discrepancies when you were reading the transcript for one entire day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure what to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're not sure that there are any differences?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: There may be in a word or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the differences are minor?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know what to say. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, let me point to you what you have stated today, and that was that you had seen Popovic on the 14th of July near the school in Orahovac. You've stated that today.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: And I also stated that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated it in your statement. You've read it, that you did?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. It's not something that I read. That's what I stated. I remember that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Are you saying that this is what you stated and you remember having stated that, or you read it in the transcript of your statement provided to you by the Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: In 2002, I stated that, and I'm sure that you can find it on the tape. I said that I wasn't 100 per cent sure, but 90 something per cent I was sure that I saw him on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated in your interview to the Prosecutor's Office that you were 99 per cent sure that you had seen Popovic in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So what remains is just 1 per cent of your uncertainty about the event?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said here that this percentage was 99.9 per cent, even higher. But let me try to see what the 1 per cent or 0.1 per cent difference consists of. On page 26 of the transcript of your interview, the Prosecutor asked you whether Popovic was in that school on the 14th. Your answer was as follows: "I'm not sure about Popovic, whether he was there or not. He was and he wasn't. I know that they were there from what other people told me." Is that what you have stated in your interview given to the Prosecutor's Office on the 13th of March?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Before you answer the question, Mr. Nicholls, I see that you are up wishing to comment or object, but I would invite to you think whether what you're going to say ought to be heard by the witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would just like English references. I think we probably got a B/C/S reference there, unless I'm confused. I also think that the witness should be able to look at the actual statement in his own language which is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you're both right on both counts. Do we have a copy of his statement in B/C/S readily available? I suppose it should be on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I believe the Defence, one team has put it into e-court but I have a hard copy available as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if you can show the hard copy that you have to Mr. Zivanovic, to make sure that we are talking of the same one, then we can let the witness see it on the ELMO. Do you agree to that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. We have a version of the interview in English, and I have been quoting from page 24. We have another version with mixed texts, the original and the translation, so B/C/S is combined with the English. I'm reading from that text because I believe that it contains the witness's original words, which I'm trying to convey to him. This is on page 26 of that interview -- of the transcript of that interview, when I quoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I quoted this text, I skipped the English translation because I thought that it would be pointless for me to read the English translation after every sentence. I just quoted his words in Serbian, in order to make things more clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Is that clear to you now, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Pretty much, yes, and I've got the copy of the transcript, the mixed one. We also have one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's in e-court so we can locate it, if we have the 65 ter number. It's there. It's there. It's there. So Madam Usher, I would like you to assist the witness to make sure that he has it on his screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could just make one point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, can you see the document on your monitor, on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Yes. I can see we can proceed, and we'll have a break in about two, three minutes' time, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could make one point for clarity for the record, and it may help my friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The transcript that the witness reviewed that was given to him to read was not this one, which is mixed, because it's a bit confusing having the English. What he had was the B/C/S version of the entire English statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. I mean, if you agree that he should see the complete text in B/C/S without these deletions of the English corresponding translation, there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I might not have been clear, Your Honour. What I mean is the transcript I gave him was only B/C/S. It had no English in it. If my friend is going to use it, I want to know it's not the one he read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon. One moment, Mr. Zivanovic, because there is Mr. Bourgon behind you. Okay. Will you try now, Mr. Bourgon. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The version that is on the screen presently is one that was prepared by our team --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- where we crossed out all of the English to ensure we had one copy with only the B/C/S, to I could avoid the problems I ran into had last time with the mixed version. My colleague is now indicating that there exists a version only with B/C/S. I would very much like to have this because it was very time consuming to prepare this copy and to scan it over again in order to have pure versions in both languages. So if there is a B/C/S-only version that exists, it would be very much appreciated if we could get it. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Bourgon, for having explained the origin of this document or of these redactions in this document. I suppose, Mr. Nicholls, if you have an entire B/C/S copy, you will make it available to the various Defence teams and not just the Nikolic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I thought it had been disclosed. If it hasn't, I am sorry and I'll make it available immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I make a suggestion? We are going to break now. Why don't we agree to give the witness the text of his statement so that he can go through it during the break while he's having a coffee, and that would, I'm sure, help us later on when we continue with Mr. Zivanovic's cross-examination, but also others cross-examinations that will be coming up. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. We have never had this transcript in B/C/S as we just now learned about. I suggest, and I'm requesting - I don't know if my other colleagues, I think, will go along with me - I believe we need at least an hour's break so we can get this copy so my client can read it in his own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I suppose you had received what we see on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But how come Mr. Bourgon had it and Ms. Nikolic had it and you didn't have it? How can it be? I don't know. I mean, I don't have an answer for it, and I'm not expected to provide one myself, but is there any other Defence team that has never seen the document that we see on the screen now before? Because I take it that this was a document that was disclosed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I might have been wrong, but I was under the impression that also the pure B/C/S transcript was. And if wasn't by mistake, I give it now, and I have no objection to an hour break if they need it. That's no problem for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have no objection, but we do. If this had been disclosed, there is no reason why a simplified version of it should result in a longer break rather than a shorter one. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could my colleague confirm that the B/C/S-only version, the B/C/S is the same as it was on the mixed, that it's not a new B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. The B/C/S version we have is the B/C/S of the English that was disclosed to them, so I cannot say that one word may not have been slightly different in the B/C/S. I haven't compared the B/C/S to the B/C/S, so I cannot affirm that. What I can confirm is that we have a full B/C/S translation of his statement in English, which is just a translation into B/C/S, and that I can provide now. It should be virtually the same, or identical, but I can't say that I've compared every line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why should there be differences? Because this is a question and answer, a question is put in English and translated to the witness or to the person making the statement in his language, so it should appear there; then he gives his answer in his own language, and the interpreter translates it and the translation appears on the document. What we have redacted here is the translation. All that was stated in the in B/C/S, either by the witness who was making the statement then or the interpreter, I don't see a reason why it should be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It should be the same, Your Honour. It's just that while this was being prepared and broken up, I don't know that the person listening to the tape didn't say this word, It's an R, it should be this way. I just can't say every word is identical, but it should be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll try to make it short, but what you see on the screen now is the original words, as they were said by the witness. What is on the version that my colleague has is a translation from the English. That's one step further. So I want to make sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why should it be that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Because it was translated from the English and not from his words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It went from the words pronounced by the witness into English, and the English was put back into B/C/S by a translator and not by original wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. This is a B/C/S transcript. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- I can give it to him in the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. Please see to this during the break. I would like the witness to be given both texts now that there is the possibility of some divergences. Mr. Nicholls, Madam Usher, Madam Registrar, who is going to look after that, the procurement? You need to see to this during the break. Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now, which means we'll start at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you have sorted out the matter we discussed briefly before the break. Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Nicholls, whoever wishes to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I believe all Defence have now been provided with the transcript, which is solely B/C/S. It shouldn't really be any kind of a problem because it's really just two versions of the transcript. The difficulty arose - I know you're probably not interested in that - because for some reason they both have exactly the same ERN, so that is why this happened. They are old transcripts, but now we've got both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Incidentally, you will have noticed the absence of Judge Stole. We are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis(A). The reason is that an urgent matter, personal matter, has cropped up to which he needed to attend to immediately. So let's proceed. Do you wish to address the Chamber, Mr. Bourgon, or do you wish to leave it at that? Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, over the break, I managed to compare the first two or three pages. It seems the two versions are identical, but still there are passages in English. For instance, on page 2, we have a passage that is half in English. The question is half in English and half in B/C/S. But, any way, I assume we should look through it a bit longer; although, I suppose it's identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can safely proceed now. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to raise an issue. I just received the B/C/S version of the transcript. I had no time to do any comparison. It's over ten pages. But in view of my line of examination, and the first answers that I got from the witness, where he said something that is in the second version of the transcript and does not feature in the first one, I don't think I can continue before we have been able to fully compare the versions, including the relevant passages that would be the subject of my cross-examination, before we establish, namely, that they are identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't object, Your Honour. We have given the witness the Court ordered copy to review, which is the pure B/C/S, that's the one he was given to review earlier by himself. So I can understand my friend's desire to compare all the passages, and I don't object to that. And I think -- I mean, it's still early in the day, but if he needs that time, I certainly have no objection. And it might even possibly save time if there is anything that matters that he wants to go back to tomorrow because he hasn't had time to review. As I say, they should be, as Madam Nikolic said, virtually identical. But if he needs more time, I don't object.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just for Your Honours' information, there will probably be time as well because once this witness is finished, if he finishes early tomorrow, earlier than the very end, the next scheduled witness can't start until Wednesday morning. I've talked to my friends and would call the investigator we tried to call last week. There wasn't enough time then, but now he would testify exactly what they were told he would testify to the, and they've got all the documents. So that was going to be our gap filler tomorrow, but it looks as though there will be close to a full day tomorrow, and that's just for Your Honours' information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Two questions; one addressed to Mr. Zivanovic, the other to the other Defence teams. Mr. Zivanovic, are there other areas or topics of your cross-examination that you can address without the need to refer to this statement, in which case we can then proceed with your cross-examination and reserve the remaining questions until later. If you could address that, if you could respond to that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my entire cross-examination has to do with discrepancies between what the witness said today and what he said earlier in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. There are other Defence teams that propose to have a short examination, and that's the Borovcanin, the Miletic, and the Pandurevic teams. Any one of you is in a position to start the cross-examination now? Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Either Stojanovic or Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. In view of the examination in chief, we will most probably have no questions. But depending on what we hear on cross-examination, we reserve the right to change our minds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In relation to this witness, I'd like to preserve my position in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Anybody else? The Beara Defence team, Mr. Meek, do you think you're in a position to start your cross-examination? You asked for 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I think it would be beneficial, since I do not speak B/C/S but my other members on my team do, to start today would be counterproductive, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Nikolic or Mr. Bourgon. I don't know who is going to address this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We take the same position, Mr. President. We need to verify. My colleague said that, of course, they may be identical, but we have found already some discrepancies and we wish to go through the full transcript in the B/C/S to check that out before we proceed. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can assure you, we appreciate that. Let me please confer with my colleagues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We fully appreciate the points raised by various the Defence teams. We fully understand that it will be more a practical approach to adjourn now, and then come back to this witness tomorrow. In the meantime, the witness can retain the copy of the statement that he has been given. Please, go through it carefully because, as I anticipate, there will be several questions which will refer you directly to what is contained in that statement of yours to the Prosecution. Okay. We stand adjourned until tomorrow afternoon at 2.15. The only day this week that we've managed to shift the sitting to the morning is Friday, the 11th. The rest of the week we have sittings in the afternoon. All right. Yes. Thank you, Judge Prost, for reminding me. Mr. Bircakovic, we have to stop here, as I'm sure you would have understood. We will continue with your testimony tomorrow. Since there is this interval of time between today and tomorrow, I want to make sure you are aware of a responsibility, of a duty, an obligation, that you have under our rules; namely, that you are not to discuss or allow anyone to discuss with you the subject matter of your testimony. In other words, you're not to discuss with anyone the matters that you are giving evidence upon. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow afternoon at 2.15. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
